thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected - service=inference-api - region=us-west-2 - 5xx rate ~48% since 2024-12-02T17:41:24Z

alex: grabbing it now. errors are all 502/504 from upstream routing to pool-7. My metrics show request queue saturation and connection resets.

sam: tagging eng-sre. can you paste the frontend router tail? wondering if new autoscaler config landed.

alex: logs: ```
[17:41:30] frontend-3 ERROR upstream reset host=model-pool-7 code=502
[17:41:33] router WARN connection pool depleted to model-pool-7
[17:41:36] frontend-6 ERROR failed handshake: EOF
```

maria: runtime noticed a config commit at 17:35 that changed per-host max-conns and lowered DNS TTL for pool discovery. rolling back DNS TTL now; investigating connection churn.

sam: can we divert traffic off pool-7 to pool-3/4 while we stabilize? need a quick weight shift to keep latency under SLO.

alex: applying emergency routing rule: shift 60% away from pool-7 over 30s. monitoring.

deploy-bot: Config rollback initiated by maria - cfg/pool-discovery v3 -> v2

jordan: customer-impact: I see 12 enterprise customers with >1000 requests in the window, some saw >30% error ratio. tagging @nate-billing for credits and @lia for contract review.

nate-billing: on it. I will pull per-customer error exposure and propose credit calculations. please hold external comms until we have numbers.

lia: quick legal note - enterprise contracts reference 'service availability' and give Redwood discretion on credits. don't promise amounts publicly.

alex: status page draft below, planning to publish once mitigation looks stable (target in 10m):

```
Status: Partial outage - Inference API (US-West-2)

We are investigating increased error rates for the Inference API in US-West-2. A recent configuration change to service discovery and connection limits is suspected. Traffic is being shifted away from the affected pool while we revert the change. Users may experience 5xx errors or increased latency. No customer data loss has been detected.

Start: 2024-12-02T17:41 UTC
Affected: API customers routing through US-West-2
Next update: 2024-12-02T17:55 UTC
```

sam: add 'no model weights or user data were modified' to reassure. also include contact for enterprise support.

alex: posted status update with that extra line. mitigation showing improvement; error rates down to ~6% after reroute and rollback.

statuspage-bot: Incident updated on status.redwood.ai - "Partial outage (mitigated)"

jordan: drafting customer notification template. keep it short and include CTA for usage report. template below:

```
Subject: Incident notice - Inference API errors in US-West-2 (Dec 2)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We experienced elevated 5xx error rates for the Inference API in US-West-2 between 17:41 and 17:52 UTC on Dec 2 due to a configuration change affecting service discovery and connection limits. We reverted the change and shifted traffic; services returned to baseline shortly after.

Impact: Some requests returned 5xx errors or experienced higher latency. Our investigation confirms no user data or model artifacts were altered.

Credits: We are calculating per-customer exposure. If your error ratio during the window exceeded thresholds defined by our incident policy, we will propose a service credit. Reply if you'd like a detailed usage report for your account.

Thanks for your patience,
Redwood Inference Ops
```

nate-billing: proposing quick triage heuristics to speed customer responses (internal only):
- exposure metric = percent of customer requests that returned 5xx during incident window
- exposure >= 25% => provisional credit = 10% of monthly invoice pro-rated by impacted minutes
- exposure 10%-25% => provisional credit = 5% pro-rated
- exposure < 10% => no credit but offer usage report on request

lia: legal okay with provisional internal heuristics but do not include exact percentages in outbound customer messages. use language like 'may be eligible for credit'.

maria: RCA quick note: root cause = aggressive reduction of DNS TTL and lowering max-conns per host; under bursty traffic this caused endpoints to be resolved too frequently and connection storms. reverted, and added an automated check to detect DNS churn > X resolutions/min and temporarily hold new commits.

sam: update runbook: auto-avoid pool when upstream connection resets >30% for 90s; also alert SRE to potential config push.

jordan: I'm preparing individualized customer exposure extracts. Nate, once you post the spreadsheet I'll send the provisional credit notes.

nate-billing: spreadsheet (internal): https://redwood.internal/sheets/INC-1769991234-exposure - contains per-account request counts, 5xx counts, and preliminary proposed credits.

alex: handing to night on-call @sam-night. I'm leaving a short handoff note in the incident doc and attaching logs. Will do a full RCA tomorrow.

sam-night: taking over monitoring. will escalate immediately if error rate >10% for more than 5 minutes.

maria: follow-up action items: 1) revert config pushed without canary gate, 2) add pre-commit lint for discovery TTL changes, 3) schedule postmortem for 48 hours with customer impact sheet attached.

alex: closing active pager for now. thanks team for quick rollback and coordinated comms. please add any outstanding follow-ups to the incident tracker. :white_check_mark:
